questions.q: What is the Spanish name for the letter H?
questions.explanation: H is called hache in Spanish, even though the h itself is always silent.

questions.q: Which Spanish vowel sounds like the ee in 'see'?
questions.explanation: i always sounds like ee — the same way every single time.

questions.q: What sound does ñ make, as in año?
options: silent, like the h in hola
questions.explanation: ñ sounds like the ny in canyon or the ni in onion.

questions.q: Perro (dog) and pero (but) sound almost the same. What's the one difference?
options: Perro has a rolled, buzzing rr; pero has a single soft r
They are pronounced exactly the same
questions.explanation: The double rr is rolled or trilled; the single r is a quick, soft tap.

questions.q: You want to ask a classmate how to spell their name. What do you say?
questions.explanation: ¿Cómo se escribe? means 'how do you spell it?'

questions.q: How would you answer if someone asked how 'Ana' is spelled?
questions.explanation: Se escribe means 'it is spelled,' followed by the letter names in order.
